verses.text: "At that time the kingdom of heaven will be like ten young bridesmaids. They took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.
Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.
The foolish ones took their lamps, but they did not take any extra oil with them.
The wise ones took oil in jars along with their lamps.
The bridegroom was a long time in coming, and they all became sleepy and fell asleep.
"At midnight someone shouted, 'Here is the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!'
"Then all the bridesmaids woke up and got their lamps ready.
The foolish ones said to the wise ones, 'Give us some of your oil. Our lamps are going out.'
"'No,' they replied. 'There may not be enough for both us and you. Go to the people who sell oil and buy some for yourselves.'
"So they went to buy the oil. But while they were away, the bridegroom arrived. The bridesmaids who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the door was shut.
"Later the other bridesmaids also came. 'Lord, Lord,' they said, 'open the door for us!'
"But he replied, 'I tell you for certain, I do not know you.'
"So keep watch, because you do not know the day or the hour when the Son of Man will come.
"It will also be like a man who was going on a journey. He called his servants and put them in charge of his money.
He gave five bags of gold to one, two bags of gold to another, and one bag of gold to another. He gave each of them as much as he knew they could handle. Then he went on his journey.
The servant who had received five bags of gold went straight away and used the money to trade. He earned five more bags.
In the same way, the one with two bags of gold earned two more.
But the servant who had received one bag went and dug a hole in the ground and hid his master's money.
"After a long time the master of those servants came back, and he settled accounts with them.
The servant who had received five bags of gold brought the other five. 'Master,' he said, 'you trusted me with five bags of gold. Look, I have earned five more.'
"His master replied, 'Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things. I will put you in charge of many things. Come and share your master's happiness!'
"The servant with two bags of gold also came. 'Master,' he said, 'you trusted me with two bags of gold. Look, I have earned two more.'
"His master replied, 'Well done, good and faithful servant! You have been faithful with a few things. I will put you in charge of many things. Come and share your master's happiness!'

"Then the servant who had received one bag of gold came. 'Master,' he said, 'I knew that you are a hard man. You harvest where you have not planted, and you gather crops where you have not scattered seed.
So I was afraid. I went out and hid your gold in the ground. Here is what belongs to you.'
"His master replied, 'You evil, lazy servant! So you knew that I harvest where I have not planted and gather crops where I have not scattered seed?
Then you should have put my money in the bank. When I came back, I would have received it back with interest.
"'Take the bag of gold from him, and give it to the one who has ten bags.
Everyone who has something will be given more, and they will have plenty. But whoever does not have anything, even what they have will be taken away from them.
Throw that useless servant outside into the darkness. There people will cry and grind their teeth.'
"When the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the angels with him, he will sit on his glorious throne.
All the nations will be gathered in front of him. He will separate the people into two groups, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
He will put the sheep on his right and the goats on his left.
"Then the King will say to those on his right, 'Come, you who are blessed by my Father. Receive the kingdom that has been prepared for you since the world was made.
I was hungry, and you gave me something to eat. I was thirsty, and you gave me something to drink. I was a stranger, and you invited me in.
I needed clothes, and you gave them to me. I was ill, and you took care of me. I was in prison, and you came to visit me.'
"Then the people who did what was right will answer him, 'Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you something to drink?
When did we see you as a stranger and invite you in, or needing clothes and give them to you?
When did we see you ill or in prison and go to visit you?'
"The King will reply, 'I tell you for certain, whatever you did for one of the least important of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.'
"Then he will say to those on his left, 'Get away from me, you who are cursed! Go into the fire that burns for ever, which has been prepared for the devil and his angels.
I was hungry, and you gave me nothing to eat. I was thirsty, and you gave me nothing to drink.
I was a stranger, and you did not invite me in. I needed clothes, and you did not give me any. I was ill and in prison, and you did not take care of me.'
"They also will answer, 'Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty, or a stranger, or needing clothes, or ill, or in prison, and did not help you?'
"He will reply, 'I tell you for certain, whatever you did not do for one of the least important of these, you did not do for me.'
"Then they will go away to be punished for ever, but the people who did what was right will go to eternal life."
